topics.title: Lenses and Optical Instruments
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: know the properties of converging and diverging lenses, and how they are used in everyday life (k, u, s)
understand how lenses are used in optical systems such as the magnifying glass, correcting sight in the human eye and in camera lenses (k, u, v/a)

body.text: A converging (convex) lens bulges outward and bends light rays inward, bringing parallel rays together at the focal point. A diverging (concave) lens curves inward and spreads light rays apart.

A converging lens can form a magnified image, which is why it is used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and to correct long sight (where the eye cannot focus on near objects). A diverging lens is used to correct short sight (where the eye cannot focus on distant objects).
The human eye itself contains a converging lens that focuses light onto the retina at the back of the eye, allowing us to see clearly.

Use the PhET Geometric Optics: Basics simulation below (Lens screen). Move an object in front of a converging lens and watch how the image forms, and how it changes as you move the object or change the lens.
